suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-33 adds this relationship only as a bounded lower-limb amputation phantom-pain association. A study of phantom limb complex after lower-limb amputation evaluated how phantom phenomena varied by amputation level, but ankle disarticulation alone does not establish phantom limb pain in every person or determine an individual's pain course. Require independently documented ankle disarticulation, documented phantom limb pain by validated assessment compatible in chronology, and specialist review. Preserve residual-limb pain, neuroma, pre-amputation pain, peripheral neuropathy, spinal pathology, and psychiatric contributors.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of ankle disarticulation, indication, level, and date
Documented phantom limb pain by validated assessment with compatible chronology
Distinction between phantom pain, residual-limb pain, neuroma, and prosthetic or wound pain
Assessment of pre-amputation pain, peripheral neuropathy, spinal pathology, and psychiatric contributors
Pain or rehabilitation specialist assessment of the individual relationship

sourceReferences.citation: Kelle B, Kozanoğlu E, Biçer ÖS, Tan İ. Association between phantom limb complex and the level of amputation in lower limb amputee. Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc. 2017;51(2):142-145. PMID 28242264. doi:10.1016/j.aott.2017.02.007.
sourceReferences.note: Lower-limb amputation evidence addressing phantom limb complex and variation by amputation level. Supports a bounded post-amputation association and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 28242264; lower-limb amputation-level analysis of phantom limb complex

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Phantom limb phenomena are reported after lower-limb amputation and vary with amputation level, but the evidence does not establish phantom limb pain in every person with ankle disarticulation or an individual nexus without documented pain, chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by lower-limb amputation-level association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Peripheral nerve transection and post-amputation sensory reorganization may generate phantom pain, but the individual pathway must be established from pain characterization, amputation records, chronology, and specialist evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Phantom limb pain is reported after lower-limb amputation, but amputation level evidence does not establish that ankle disarticulation caused or aggravated phantom pain in every individual; pain phenotype, chronology, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented ankle disarticulation and phantom pain; amputation level and chronology; validated pain phenotype; residual-limb, neuroma, pre-amputation, neuropathic, spinal, and psychiatric alternatives; specialist assessment
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Residual-limb pain, neuroma, wound pain, or prosthetic fit problems
Pre-amputation pain, peripheral neuropathy, or spinal pathology
Psychiatric, sleep, medication, or other coexisting pain contributors
